Classic Fiction.author: George Orwell
Classic Fiction.description: A dystopian social science fiction novel and cautionary tale. The story follows the life of Winston Smith, a low-ranking member of 'the Party'.
Classic Fiction.authorBio: George Orwell (Eric Arthur Blair) was an English novelist and critic known for his opposition to totalitarianism.
Classic Fiction.introWhy: Orwell wrote the book to warn Western nations of the dangers of totalitarian regimes and expansionist surveillance states.
Classic Fiction.introHow: He composed the manuscript on the isolated Scottish island of Jura while battling severe tuberculosis and physically writing long hours.
Classic Fiction.introWhat: A chilling dystopian projection of a world ruled by constant surveillance, cognitive doublethink, and total party control.

Classic Fiction.title: Pride and Prejudice
Classic Fiction.author: Jane Austen
Classic Fiction.description: A classic romantic novel of manners following Elizabeth Bennet as she navigates issues of morality, family reputation, and marriage with the haughty Mr. Darcy.

Classic Fiction.title: Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus
Classic Fiction.author: Mary Wollstonecraft Shelley
Classic Fiction.description: The seminal gothic science-fiction masterpiece relating Victor Frankenstein's audacious experiment in creating life and the tragic aftermath of abandonment.

Classic Fiction.title: Moby Dick; Or, The Whale
Classic Fiction.author: Herman Melville
Classic Fiction.description: Ishmael's profound narrative of Captain Ahab's obsessive pursuit of the white whale Moby Dick aboard the ill-fated whaleship Pequod.

Classic Fiction.title: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland
Classic Fiction.author: Lewis Carroll
Classic Fiction.description: The celebrated fantasy classic following young Alice as she tumbles down a rabbit hole into a whimsical subterranean world of anthropomorphic creatures.

Classic Fiction.title: Dracula
Classic Fiction.author: Bram Stoker
Classic Fiction.description: The foundational vampire horror masterpiece told through journals and letters as Count Dracula attempts to establish an empire in Victorian England.

Classic Fiction.title: Middlemarch
Classic Fiction.author: George Eliot
Classic Fiction.description: A panorama of provincial 19th-century English life following Dorothea Brooke and Dr. Tertius Lydgate through idealism, romance, and compromise.

Classic Fiction.title: A Tale of Two Cities
Classic Fiction.author: Charles Dickens
Classic Fiction.description: Historical novel depicting London and Paris during the Reign of Terror, culminating in Sydney Carton's heroic act of self-sacrifice.

Classic Fiction.title: The Great Gatsby
Classic Fiction.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
Classic Fiction.description: The quintessential novel of the Roaring Twenties examining wealth, obsession, and the decay of the American Dream on Long Island's North Shore.

Classic Fiction.title: A Room with a View
Classic Fiction.author: E. M. Forster
Classic Fiction.description: A lighthearted critique of Edwardian propriety following young Lucy Honeychurch as she chooses between passionate freedom and social convention.

Classic Fiction.title: The Odyssey
Classic Fiction.author: Homer
Classic Fiction.description: Homer's timeless ancient Greek epic recounting the ten-year journey of Odysseus returning home to Ithaca after the fall of Troy.

Classic Fiction.title: War and Peace
Classic Fiction.author: Leo Tolstoy
Classic Fiction.description: Tolstoy's sweeping epic chronicling Russian society, philosophical destiny, and military conflict throughout the Napoleonic invasion of 1812.

Classic Fiction.title: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz
Classic Fiction.author: L. Frank Baum
Classic Fiction.description: The timeless American fairy tale following Dorothy and Toto as they journey along the yellow brick road to meet the Wizard of Oz.

Classic Fiction.title: Adventures of Huckleberry Finn
Classic Fiction.author: Mark Twain
Classic Fiction.description: Mark Twain's literary triumph chronicling Huck Finn and Jim's raft journey down the Mississippi River in search of freedom and humanity.

Classic Fiction.title: Ulysses
Classic Fiction.author: James Joyce
Classic Fiction.description: The landmark modernist masterpiece following Leopold Bloom's odyssey through the streets of Dublin on June 16, 1904.

Classic Fiction.title: The Time Machine
Classic Fiction.author: H. G. Wells
Classic Fiction.description: The foundational time-travel science fiction novella uncovering the distant evolutionary fate of humanity in the year 802,701 AD.

Classic Fiction.title: Anne of Green Gables
Classic Fiction.author: L. M. Montgomery
Classic Fiction.description: The heartwarming tale of imaginative orphan Anne Shirley as she transforms the lives of Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert in Avonlea.

Classic Fiction.title: The Scarlet Letter
Classic Fiction.author: Nathaniel Hawthorne
Classic Fiction.description: A somber examination of guilt, vengeance, and redemption in 17th-century Puritan Boston centered on Hester Prynne and the embroidered letter 'A'.

Classic Fiction.title: The Best Short Stories of 1917
Classic Fiction.author: Edward J. O'Brien (Editor)
Classic Fiction.description: An authentic yearbook and curated collection of outstanding American short fiction from 1917 reflecting contemporary wartime themes and literary artistry.

Classic Fiction.title: The Brothers Karamazov
Classic Fiction.author: Fyodor Dostoyevsky
Classic Fiction.description: A profound theological and psychological drama exploring faith, free will, patricide, and moral responsibility among three disparate brothers in Imperial Russia.

Classic Fiction.title: Wuthering Heights
Classic Fiction.author: Emily Brontë
Classic Fiction.description: Emily Brontë's masterpiece of Gothic romance, passionate obsession, and generational vengeance set against the brooding Yorkshire moors, following the tumultuous relationship between Heathcliff and Catherine Earnshaw.

Fantasy & Sci-Fi.title: Dune
Fantasy & Sci-Fi.author: Frank Herbert
Fantasy & Sci-Fi.description: Set on the desert planet Arrakis, Dune is the story of the boy Paul Atreides, heir to a noble family tasked with ruling an inhospitable world.
Fantasy & Sci-Fi.disclaimer-text: This copy of Dune is shared for limited educational critique and literary review under fair use guidelines. All rights reserved by the author's estate.

Fantasy & Sci-Fi.title: The Lord of the Rings Collection
Fantasy & Sci-Fi.author: J.R.R. Tolkien
Fantasy & Sci-Fi.description: The classic fantasy trilogy following the quest to destroy the One Ring.

Fantasy & Sci-Fi.title: The Hobbit
Fantasy & Sci-Fi.author: J.R.R. Tolkien
Fantasy & Sci-Fi.description: A great modern classic and the prelude to The Lord of the Rings. Bilbo Baggins is a hobbit who enjoys a comfortable, unambitious life.

General Resources.title: Mathematical Facts, Constants & Formulas
General Resources.author: Hesten's Learning Reference Series
General Resources.description: The definitive 12-chapter mathematical reference handbook spanning Grade 1 to Grade 12. Covers all standard curricula, core theorems, formula cards, mental math hacks, and grade-level cheat sheets with full MathJax typesetting.
General Resources.authorBio: Hesten's Learning Editorial Mathematics Guild — developed by educators, mathematicians, and typographers to produce an authoritative, gold-standard reference handbook across Grade 1 through Grade 12 mathematics.
General Resources.introWhy: To provide students, teachers, and independent scholars with an unambiguous, publication-grade mathematical handbook featuring rigorous definitions, axiomatic theorems, exact formulas, mental math hacks, and dynamic LaTeX/MathJax typesetting.
General Resources.introHow: Systematically structured into 12 grade-level volumes (Grade 1 through Grade 12), each containing all core curriculum standards, worked problem models, pitfall warnings, study shortcuts, and comprehensive summary cheat sheets.
General Resources.introWhat: A comprehensive 12-volume reference handbook featuring over 250+ formal theorems, definitions, step-by-step worked solutions, exact trigonometric tables, prime factorizations, derivative and integral rosters, and high-speed mental math hacks.

General Resources.title: Chambers's Twentieth Century Dictionary (Part 1: A-D)
General Resources.author: Thomas Davidson (Editor)
General Resources.description: Comprehensive reference lexicon documenting English vocabulary, pronunciation, etymology, and historical usage from Letter A through Letter D.

General Resources.title: The King James Version of the Bible
General Resources.author: King James Translators (Authorized Version)
General Resources.description: The Authorized King James Version of the Holy Bible, originally published in 1611 under the auspices of King James I of England. Containing all 66 books of the Old and New Testaments, renowned for its profound impact on English literature, idiom, and rhetoric.

ELA.title: The Complete Works of William Shakespeare
ELA.author: William Shakespeare
ELA.description: The monumental collection of 37 plays, sonnets, and poetic works by the foremost dramatist of the English Renaissance.

ELA.title: Romeo and Juliet
ELA.author: William Shakespeare
ELA.description: Shakespeare's celebrated tragedy of young star-crossed lovers whose passionate devotion transcends their families' ancient feud.

ELA.title: Spoon River Anthology
ELA.author: Edgar Lee Masters
ELA.description: A pioneering collection of free-verse epitaph poems spoken from beyond the grave by the former inhabitants of the fictional town of Spoon River.

ELA.title: The Works of William Shakespeare (Cambridge Ed., Vol. 5)
ELA.author: William Shakespeare
ELA.description: Authoritative Cambridge critical edition featuring Henry VI (Parts 1, 2, and 3) and Richard III with full scholarly collation.

ELA.title: The Works of William Shakespeare (Cambridge Ed., Vol. 7)
ELA.author: William Shakespeare
ELA.description: Scholarly Cambridge critical edition containing Timon of Athens, Julius Caesar, Macbeth, and Hamlet with full historical textual commentary.

Civics.title: History of Woman Suffrage, Volume III
Civics.author: Susan B. Anthony, Matilda Joslyn Gage, Elizabeth Cady Stanton
Civics.description: Comprehensive primary historical chronicle documenting the national conventions, legal campaigns, and state battles for women's voting rights from 1876 to 1885.

Civics.title: The Republic
Civics.author: Plato
Civics.description: Plato's paramount philosophical dialogue examining justice, the structure of the ideal city-state, the allegory of the cave, and the philosopher-king.

Civics.title: Second Treatise of Government
Civics.author: John Locke
Civics.description: Foundational political philosophy asserting that civil government derives legitimate authority from the consent of the governed to protect life, liberty, and property.

Civics.title: On Liberty
Civics.author: John Stuart Mill
Civics.description: A landmark philosophical treatise championing individual freedom of thought and expression, formulating the foundational harm principle.

Civics.title: The Declaration of Independence of the United States of America
Civics.author: Thomas Jefferson & The Continental Congress
Civics.description: The foundational charter of American liberty adopted on July 4, 1776, announcing the separation of the thirteen united colonies from Great Britain and declaring the self-evident truth that all people are endowed with unalienable rights to life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness.

Civics.title: The United States Bill of Rights
Civics.author: United States Congress & James Madison
Civics.description: The first ten amendments to the United States Constitution ratified in 1791, safeguarding vital American liberties including freedom of speech, religion, press, assembly, due process of law, and powers reserved to the states and the people.

Civics.title: The United States Constitution
Civics.author: United States Constitutional Convention
Civics.description: The supreme law of the United States of America established in 1787, delineating the legislative, executive, and judicial branches of the federal government and setting the foundational constitutional structure of the American Republic.

Civics.title: Give Me Liberty or Give Me Death
Civics.author: Patrick Henry
Civics.description: Patrick Henry's stirring oration delivered before the Second Virginia Convention at St. John's Church in Richmond on March 23, 1775, galvanizing the American colonies toward revolution with his timeless rallying cry: 'Give me liberty or give me death!'

Civics.title: Give Me Liberty or Give Me Death (Audio Edition)
Civics.author: Patrick Henry (LibriVox Narration)
Civics.description: Public domain audio recording and synchronized spoken word transcript of Patrick Henry's immortal 1775 address, featuring streaming MP3 narration from Project Gutenberg EBook #20046.

World History.title: The Life of Charles Dickens (Vol. I-III Complete)
World History.author: John Forster
World History.description: The definitive biography of Charles Dickens written by his closest literary confidant, offering intimate insight into his creative genius.

World History.title: The Letters of Queen Victoria (Vol. 2, 1844-1853)
World History.author: Queen Victoria
World History.description: Primary historical correspondence of Queen Victoria detailing European political upheavals of 1848, diplomatic relations, and Victorian governance.

Science.title: The Geology of Button Bay State Park
Science.author: Harry W. Dodge
Science.description: An illustrated field guide exploring the geologic history, Champlain Sea clay deposits, button stones (concretions), and ancient sedimentary formations along Lake Champlain at Button Bay State Park, Vermont.

Science.title: The Geology of Calvin Coolidge State Forest
Science.author: Harry W. Dodge
Science.description: A comprehensive geological exploration of Vermont's Calvin Coolidge State Forest Park, detailing metamorphic schists and gneisses, gold panning in Plymouth, talc and asbestos mining, and roadside field trips.

Science.title: The Geology of Darling State Park
Science.author: Harry W. Dodge
Science.description: A field study of the origins of Burke Mountain and Darling State Park in Vermont's Northeast Kingdom, examining granitic intrusions, metamorphic hornfels, glacial erratics, and scenic geological hiking trails.

Science.title: The Geology of D.A.R. State Park, Mt. Philo State Forest Park, Sand Bar State Park
Science.author: Harry W. Dodge
Science.description: A tripartite investigation of three distinctive Vermont state parks across the Champlain Valley, uncovering Crown Point limestone fossils at D.A.R. Park, the Champlain thrust fault at Mt. Philo, and the delta sands of the Lamoille River at Sand Bar Park.

Science.title: The Geology of Groton State Forest
Science.author: Robert A. Christman
Science.description: An analysis of the Knox Mountain granite pluton, glacial roche moutonnées, pegmatite dikes, and scenic mountain overlooks across Groton State Forest in Caledonia and Washington Counties, Vermont.

Science.title: The Geology of Mt. Mansfield State Forest
Science.author: Robert A. Christman
Science.description: A geologic survey of Vermont's highest peak, detailing the Camels Hump Group schists, Smugglers Notch glacial canyon, alpine periglacial features, and mountain crest structures in Mount Mansfield State Forest.

US History.title: The Green Mountain Boys : or, Vermont and the New York land jobbers
US History.author: Philip H. Smith
US History.description: An authoritative 19th-century history of Ethan Allen and the Green Mountain Boys, their fierce resistance against the New York colonial land jobbers, the capture of Fort Ticonderoga, and the founding of the independent Republic of Vermont.

US History.title: Vermont: A Study of Independence
US History.author: Rowland Evans Robinson
US History.description: Rowland E. Robinson's classic American Commonwealths volume chronicling the history of Vermont from the French and Indian Wars and New Hampshire Grants dispute, through the American Revolution, admission as the 14th state, and the Civil War.

US History.title: Vermont riflemen in the war for the union, 1861 to 1865 : A history of Company F, First United States sharp shooters
US History.author: William Y. W. Ripley
US History.description: A firsthand regimental history of Company F, 1st U.S. Sharpshooters (Berdan's Sharpshooters) written by Lt. Col. William Y. W. Ripley, covering their marksmanship trials, the Peninsular Campaign, Antietam, Fredericksburg, Chancellorsville, and Gettysburg.
